items.title: The Remaining Six Links Defended the Same Way, Down to Old Age and Death

items.zh: 問：觸以三和為緣，何故此中但說六處為緣？答：若有六處，定有餘二無闕故。又六處勝故，由六處攝二種故。問：若自所逼迫，若他所逼迫，若時候變異，若先業所引，皆得生受；何故此中但顯觸為彼緣？答：觸是彼近因故，由觸所引故；餘緣所生受亦從觸生故，必不離觸，是故偏說。
items.en: Question: Contact is conditioned by the meeting of the three — faculty, object, and consciousness — why does this teaching name only the six sense-bases? Answer: Wherever the six bases are present, the other two are guaranteed present as well; and the six bases are simply the most decisive of the three, since they already include the other two. Question: Feeling can arise from self-inflicted pressure, from pressure inflicted by another, from a change of season, or from past karma — why does this teaching name only contact as its condition? Answer: Contact is feeling's nearest cause; feeling is always brought about through contact, and whatever other condition produces feeling still does so only by way of contact, which is never absent.

items.zh: 問：經中亦說無明為緣生愛，順愛境界亦得為緣，何故此中但說受為緣耶？答：以受力故，於相似境，或求和合，或求乖離。由愚癡力，但於諸受起盡等相不如實知，由此不能制御其心。
items.en: Question: The sūtras also say that craving is conditioned by ignorance, and that a pleasing object can itself serve as its condition — why does this teaching name only feeling? Answer: It is by the very force of feeling that one seeks union with, or seeks separation from, whatever resembles it. Through the force of delusion alone, one fails to truly know feeling's own arising and ceasing, and is thereby left unable to govern the mind at all — ignorance may lie behind this, but feeling remains the nearest cause.

items.zh: 問：由隨眠未斷，順彼諸法取皆得生，何故此中但說愛為取緣？答：由希望生故，於追求時，能發隨眠，及能引彼隨順法故。問：前已說無明為緣發起業有，何故今者說取緣有？答：由取力故，即令彼業於彼彼生處能引識、名色等果。
items.en: Question: Since the latent tendencies remain unsevered, grasping in all its forms could arise from them directly — why does this teaching name only craving as grasping's condition? Answer: It is craving's own longing that, in the very act of seeking its object, awakens the latent tendencies and draws grasping's other conditions into play. Question: It was already said that ignorance conditions the arising of karmic becoming — why now say that grasping conditions becoming? Answer: It is specifically grasping's own force that causes that karma to actually project consciousness, name-and-form, and the rest of its result into a given place of rebirth.

items.zh: 問：生亦以精血等為緣，何故此中唯說有緣生耶？答：由有有故，定有餘緣無闕。又有勝故，唯說彼為緣。問：亦由遠行、不避不平等、他所逼迫為緣，老死可得，何故此中但說生緣老死耶？答：雖由彼諸緣，必以生為根本故。縱闕彼緣，但生為緣，定有老死故。
items.en: Question: Birth, too, is conditioned by parental blood and semen — why does this teaching name only becoming as birth's condition? Answer: Wherever becoming is present, every other necessary condition is guaranteed present as well, and becoming is simply the most decisive. Question: Old age and death can also come from a hard journey, from failing to avoid danger, or from being harmed by another — why does this teaching name only birth as their condition? Answer: Whatever other conditions may be involved, birth remains their root — even lacking every other condition, birth alone is enough to guarantee that old age and death will follow.

items.title: The Twelve Links Sorted into Three Paths: Affliction, Karma, and Suffering

items.zh: 問：此十二支，幾是煩惱道？幾是業道？幾是苦道？答：三是煩惱道，二是業道，餘是苦道。
items.en: Question: Of these twelve links, how many belong to the path of affliction? How many to the path of karma? How many to the path of suffering? Answer: Three belong to the path of affliction; two belong to the path of karma; the remainder belong to the path of suffering.

items.title: Cause Alone, Result Alone, or Both — and Why Nine of the Twelve Links Overlap

items.zh: 問：幾唯是因，幾唯是果，幾通因果？答：初一唯因，後一唯果，餘通因果。又即於此問，更作餘答：三唯是因，二唯是果，當知所餘亦因亦果。
items.en: Question: How many links are purely a cause? How many purely a result? How many are both? Answer: The first alone is purely a cause; the last alone is purely a result; the rest are both. And on this same question, a further answer may be given: three are purely a cause, two are purely a result, and the remainder should be understood as both.

items.zh: 問：幾是獨相，幾是雜相？答：三是獨相，行等是雜相。問：何故行、有是雜相？答：由二種說故。謂能引愛非愛果故，及能生趣差別故。問：何故識與名色、六處一分有雜相？答：由三種說故。謂依雜染時故，依潤時故，依轉時故。
items.en: Question: How many links stand alone, distinct from every other? How many overlap with another? Answer: Three stand alone; formations and the rest overlap. Question: Why do formations and becoming overlap? Answer: Because both are spoken of two ways — as projecting a desirable or undesirable result, and as generating the specific destiny that result belongs to. Question: Why do consciousness, name-and-form, and part of the six bases overlap? Answer: Because consciousness is spoken of three ways — at the time it is defiled, at the time it is moistened, and at the time it actively operates.

items.zh: 問：何故識乃至受，與老死有雜相？答：由二種說故。謂別顯苦相故，及顯引生差別故。
items.en: Question: Why are consciousness through feeling mixed in characteristics with old age and death? Answer: Because of two ways of teaching: to show separately the characteristic of suffering, and to show the differences in projecting and producing.

items.title: Four Meanings of "Condition" Revisited, and the Twelve Links Sorted into Suffering and Its Origin

items.zh: 復次，於緣起中：云何數往義？謂生已不住義。云何和合義？謂諸緣聚集義。云何起義？謂諸緣和合之所引攝新新生義。云何緣起？云何緣生？謂諸行生起法性，是名緣起；即彼生已，說名緣生。
items.en: Further, within dependent origination, what is meant by repeated going? That once arisen, nothing remains standing still. What is meant by gathering? The very gathering together of conditions. What is meant by arising? What that gathering of conditions draws in and brings to fresh, ever-new arising. What is dependent origination, and what is dependently arisen? The very nature of formations coming to be at all is called dependent origination; and that same thing, once it has actually come to be, is called what has dependently arisen.

items.zh: 問：幾支苦諦攝及現法為苦？答：二，謂生及老死。問：幾支苦諦攝，當來為苦？答：識乃至受種子性。問：幾支集諦攝？答：所餘支。
items.en: Question: How many links belong to the truth of suffering, as suffering already present in this life? Answer: Two — birth and old-age-and-death. Question: How many links belong to the truth of suffering, as suffering yet to come? Answer: The seed-nature of consciousness through feeling. Question: How many links belong to the truth of suffering's origin? Answer: All the rest.

blocks.text: A shorter reading, finishing the defence of the links' order and then sorting the twelve links in several ways: into the three paths of affliction, karma, and suffering; into causes and results; and into the noble truths. These groupings are the ones most Buddhist teachers use when they explain the twelve links, so they are worth fixing in memory.

The same reasoning as yesterday is carried down to old age and death. The order of the links is not arbitrary: each step is the one that must come next in the process of projecting and generating a life.
The twelve links fall into three **paths** (三道):

Master Cháng Bǎi's image: "Affliction is like a dragon. As a dragon guards a pool so that its water flows forever, never drying, affliction guards karma so that it bears results without end." Karma alone would run dry; affliction keeps it flowing.

Some links are only causes, some only results, and most are both. Venerable Miào Jìng: ignorance, craving, and grasping are purely causes, "the root that initiates karma and moistens rebirth": ignorance initiates, craving and grasping moisten. Birth and old age and death are purely results. The other seven are both, which is why nine of the twelve overlap in their roles.

subs.head: Dependent origination and the dependently arisen

blocks.text: The treatise distinguishes **dependent origination** (緣起) from the **dependently arisen** (緣生). Venerable Miào Jìng: "Dependent origination speaks from the side of cause; dependently arisen from the side of result." The same twelve links can be seen as the process of conditioning or as the things conditioned.

subs.head: The links and the noble truths

blocks.text: Which links belong to the truth of suffering? Birth and old age and death are present suffering; the seed-nature of consciousness through feeling is future suffering. All the rest, ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, becoming, belong to the truth of **origin**. Master Cháng Bǎi adds: cessation and the path are not among the links at all; they are what ends them.

This sorting makes the four truths concrete. "Suffering" is not a mood but these particular links; "origin" is not a vague cause but these particular links, which, being afflictions and karma, can be cut.

quiz.q: How many of the twelve links belong to the paths of affliction, karma, and suffering?
options: three affliction (ignorance, craving, grasping), two karma (formations, becoming), the other seven suffering
quiz.why: "Three belong to the path of affliction; two belong to the path of karma; the remainder belong to the path of suffering." Master Cháng Bǎi's mnemonic: ignorance, craving, grasping — affliction; formations, becoming — karma; consciousness to feeling plus birth and old age — suffering.

quiz.q: Master Cháng Bǎi says "affliction is like a dragon." What does he mean?
options: as a dragon guards a pool so its water never dries, affliction guards karma so it bears results endlessly
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Affliction is like a dragon — as a dragon guards a pool so its water flows forever, never drying, affliction guards karma so it yields results without end." Karma is like a medicinal herb: once its fruit ripens, it's spent.

quiz.q: The second answer says three are purely causes and two purely results. Which three, and why, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: ignorance, craving, grasping — the roots that initiate karma and moisten rebirth
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'The three are ignorance, craving, grasping — the root that initiates karma and moistens rebirth': initiating is ignorance, moistening is craving and grasping." The two pure results are birth and old-age-and-death. Master Cháng Bǎi: ignorance defiles the other eleven but isn't defiled by them.

quiz.q: The text distinguishes "dependent origination" from "dependently arisen." How does Venerable Miào Jìng put it?
options: dependent origination speaks of the cause; dependently arisen, the result
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "So dependent origination speaks from the side of cause, dependently arisen from the side of result." Master Cháng Bǎi: the cause is "this existing, that exists"; the result "this arising, that arises."

quiz.q: Which links belong to the truth of suffering as present suffering, and which as future suffering?
options: birth and old age-death are present suffering; the seed-nature of consciousness through feeling is future suffering; the rest belong to origin
quiz.why: "Two — birth and old-age-and-death. … The seed-nature of consciousness through feeling. … All the rest." Master Cháng Bǎi: cessation and path aren't mentioned, as they belong to the reversal, not transmigration.
